note: Login History records one row per successful login into a dedicated login_history base table (uid, login timestamp, hostname/IP, user_agent, one_time flag) via hook_user_login(). Retention is bounded by the single config value login_history.settings:keep_user (default 50; 0 = keep all), pruned at login time and on cron. Data is surfaced via a Views base table (login_history joined to users_field_data), two report routes (/admin/reports/login-history for perm 'view all login histories'; /user/{user}/login-history for 'view own login history'), and the last_login_block block plugin. Introspection cases read live config (keep_user) and the live login_history table; execution cases set the retention config and place the last_login_block, both verified against live state.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with the login_history module, where is each user login recorded, and which hook writes that record? Name the storage and the hook.
evals.expected_output: Each successful login is inserted as a row into the module's own login_history database table by hook_user_login() (login_history_user_login), capturing uid, login timestamp, hostname (IP), user_agent, and a one_time flag.

evals.prompt: How do I limit how many login records login_history keeps per user, and what is the default? What config key controls it?
evals.expected_output: The config object login_history.settings has a single key keep_user (default 50). It caps rows per user; 0 keeps all. Pruning to the limit happens at login time and on cron (hook_cron). Set it at /admin/config/people/login-history or with drush cset login_history.settings keep_user <n>.

evals.prompt: Which pages does login_history provide to view login history, and which permissions gate them?
evals.expected_output: Site-wide report at /admin/reports/login-history (permission 'view all login histories', route login_history.report, backed by the login_history View), and a per-user report at /user/{user}/login-history (permission 'view own login history', route login_history.user_report). A 'Last login' block (last_login_block) is also provided.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, login_history has been configured with a specific per-user retention limit. Inspect the live configuration and state the current value of keep_user.
evals.expected_output: keep_user is 13 in login_history.settings (drush cget login_history.settings keep_user).

evals.prompt: This site's login_history table has a recorded login for user 1. Inspect the live login_history table and report the IP address (hostname) stored for that user's most recent recorded login.
evals.expected_output: The hostname is 198.51.100.42 (SELECT hostname FROM login_history WHERE uid=1 ORDER BY login DESC LIMIT 1).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure login_history to keep at most 10 login records per user, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: login_history.settings:keep_user is set to 10 (drush cset login_history.settings keep_user 10 -y, or via /admin/config/people/login-history).

evals.prompt: Place login_history's 'Last login' block into a region of the site's default theme, so authenticated users see when they last logged in. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: An enabled block config entity using plugin last_login_block is created in the default theme (e.g. Block::create(['id'=>'...','theme'=><default>,'region'=>'content','plugin'=>'last_login_block', ...])->save(), or via /admin/structure/block).
